subtype: Approach: changing the game when guests look bored [Revision]
passage:
Friday. Disha wrote her birthday plan: a game with chairs, quiet and neat, and cake after. She liked how tidy it looked.

Saturday. Ten friends sat in a ring. Two minutes in, Meera was yawning, someone kept peeking at the garden, and a boy tapped his feet. Disha looked around and put the whistle down. "New game! Catch the ribbon in the garden!" The chairs stayed in the hall and everybody ran outside, shouting.

Sunday. Gopika phoned. "That garden game was the best part. Can we play it at my house?"

qa.q: What did Disha change the game to when the chairs stopped working?
qa.a: Disha switched to catching the ribbon in the garden.

qa.q: What did Disha notice about her friends during the quiet game, and what might Disha feel?
qa.a: Disha noticed yawning, peeking at the garden and tapping feet; Disha probably felt worried the party was going flat but decided quickly.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Disha have used, and why?
qa.a: Disha could have prepared one quiet and one active game in advance, so a switch would be easy. Having a spare game means the party need not depend on a single idea.

qa.q: What did the change mean for Gopika?
qa.a: Gopika enjoyed the garden game most and wants to play it again, so for Gopika the switch saved the afternoon.

grounding: At the party the quiet game falls flat, so the birthday girl notices restless friends and changes to an active game outdoors.

subtype: Approach: changing the game when guests look bored [Revision]
passage: Jahnavi, don't worry if a game flops at your party. Let your Grandma Lalremsiami tell you about my eleventh birthday in Aizawl. I had planned a quiet game: everyone sits in a circle of chairs and passes a whisper along. By the second round my friends were yawning, one was picking at her chair, two boys were poking each other. I saw it, and my stomach sank. So I stood up and said, 'Everyone outside! Catch-the-hen!' We ran round the garden, between the orange trees, shrieking, until my mother called us in for cake. Nobody remembered the whisper game. Everybody remembered the running.

qa.q: Where did they run during the new game?
qa.a: Round the garden, between the orange trees.

qa.q: How did young Lalremsiami feel when she saw her friends yawning?
qa.a: Her stomach sank, so she felt worried and disappointed that her quiet game was falling flat.

qa.q: What choice in the story saved the party?
qa.a: Noticing her restless friends and switching straight to a running game outside, instead of pushing on with the whisper game.

qa.q: How did the friends seem to feel once they were outside?
qa.a: They were shrieking and running until cake, so they seemed happy and lively again.

grounding: Shows a birthday girl noticing restless friends during a quiet chair game and switching to a running game in the garden.

subtype: Approach: changing the game when guests look bored [Revision]
passage: The power cut came ten minutes into Binita's party, so there was no music for musical chairs. Binita switched to a quiet chair game: sit in a circle and guess who's hiding the button. By round two, Hrithik was drumming on his chair, two girls were whispering by the window, and someone had started counting the blades of the stopped fan. Binita noticed. Her stomach dropped: this was her party. Then she looked at the garden, still bright in the evening light. "New game! Chain tag, outside!" Chairs scraped. Within a minute eight kids were racing round the guava tree, Hrithik leading the chain, and Binita's laugh was the loudest.

qa.q: Why was there no music for musical chairs?
qa.a: The power cut came ten minutes into the party.

qa.q: How did Binita feel when she noticed the restless guests?
qa.a: Her stomach dropped, so she felt worried and upset that her own party was falling flat.

qa.q: What else could Binita keep ready for another power cut?
qa.a: A couple of games that need no music, like chain tag or a treasure hunt; spotting restlessness and switching quickly is what saved the evening.

qa.q: How did the switch feel for Hrithik?
qa.a: Hrithik went from drumming bored on his chair to leading the chain, so he seemed much happier 🎉

grounding: Illustrates a birthday girl seeing her chair game fall flat, noticing restless guests, and switching to a running game in the garden.
